newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland urges bail for pregnant bomb suspect.
newsitem.headline: Ireland urges bail for pregnant bomb suspect.

text.p: Ireland's deputy prime minister summoned Britain's ambassador on Wednesday to press for bail for a pregnant prisoner who is awaiting extradition to Germany to face charges over an IRA bombing.
Dick Spring said he had also queried Britain's decision to hold 25-year-old Roisin McAliskey in a high security prison in London.

"She is seven months pregnant. I believe she is entitled to certain basic decency in terms of the conditions she is held under. Also I don't think that she is a threat in relation to escape," Spring said after meeting British ambassador Veronica Sutherland.
McAliskey, the daugher of Bernadette McAliskey, nee Devlin, a Northern Irish republican and former member of Britain's parliament, was arrested late last year.
Germany wants her extradited to face charges over an Irish Republican Army bombing in June 1996 of a British army barracks at Osnabrueck. The courts have refused her repeated requests for bail.
"The question of bail is obviously a matter for the courts, but I would say that in normal circumstances in a case like this, there is no danger that she is going to try to escape," Spring said.
Irish sources said that during the meeting Spring had "underlined the widespread humanitarian concern that exists" in Ireland about the case.
Spring said he believed ambassador Sutherland was sympathetic and receptive to his remarks.
